name: AI in Safety Case Processing
blurb: Automating intake and processing of adverse event reports.
title: AI in Safety Case Processing
answer: Processing individual safety case reports is the largest cost in pharmacovigilance, by some estimates up to two thirds of a company's safety budget, and case volumes grow every year. Machine learning was shown early on to extract key case information and judge case validity from historical data, which is why intake and triage were among the first AI uses in the function.

reading.body:
Case processing is the largest cost in pharmacovigilance, and machine learning was applied to intake and triage before most other safety tasks.

The economics explain the order of adoption. If individual case reports consume up to two thirds of a safety budget, then any automation that reduces handling time per report attacks the dominant cost line rather than a marginal one. Case volumes rise every year, so the pressure compounds. The 2019 work cited here showed machine learning could extract key case information and judge case validity from historical database content, which is exactly the intake and triage step, and that is why those functions went first.

The boundary the data draws is between clerical work and medical judgement. Intake, translation, and duplicate checks are the recommended automation targets. Seriousness and causality stay with qualified staff. That split is not a limitation of the technology so much as a statement about where the liability sits, and it is the reason safety AI looks different from AI in functions where a wrong output is merely expensive.

What this does not cover is scale. There is no count of reports processed, no accuracy figure, no cost saved, and no named system in production. The evidence here is a single 2019 study plus a recommendation, so it establishes that the approach works and where it belongs, not how far it has been deployed.

terms.line: The field of computer science dedicated to creating systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence: understanding language, recognizing patterns, making decisions.

The subset of AI focused on systems that learn from data and improve with experience rather than following explicitly programmed rules. Nearly everything called AI in production is machine learning underneath.

explainer:
An individual case safety report describes one patient, one or more suspect medicines and one or more adverse events. Processing it means receiving it from wherever it arrived, checking it meets the minimum criteria to be valid, finding duplicates, entering the details into the safety database, coding drugs and events to standard dictionaries such as MedDRA, writing a narrative, assessing seriousness and expectedness, and submitting it to regulators within deadlines as short as 15 days for serious unexpected cases.

Most of those steps are rule based and repetitive, which made case processing an early target for automation and later machine learning. Today AI handles intake from emails and forms, translation, data extraction, coding suggestions and narrative drafts, with people reviewing and making the medical judgements. The goal is to keep up with growing volumes and meet deadlines without lowering quality.

developments.text: A study in Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics showed machine learning could extract case information and identify valid safety cases from historical database content, calling case processing the strongest cost driver in pharmacovigilance.
